heading:
Lapunti Arnis
De Abanico
intro: A multi-weapon-oriented Filipino combative system that originated from Cebu, Philippines. Lapunti is engineered to overwhelm opponents using rapid-fire combinations, and by pairing two of its most unique and deceptive features: abanico (fan) strikes and the cross-legged stance or footwork.

characteristics.title: Abanico Strikes
characteristics.description: Rapid fan-like combinations that strikes from unexpected angles and goes around common blocks or positions of defense. Honed through decades of experimentation and testing in actual combat or fight challenges.

characteristics.title: Cross-Legged Footwork
characteristics.description: The only FMA style that traditionally employs this type of stance and footwork. Enabling a practitioner to swiftly close or create distance, evade or gain a more advantageous position, effectively deal with multiple opponents, and fight in tight spaces.

founders: Developed during the early 1900s by the Caburnay family: Arsenio Caburnay, GM Felimon Caburnay, and SGM Prudencio 'Undo' Caburnay, with significant contributions from GM Johnny Chiuten, a master of Choy Li Fut Kung Fu and other arnis styles. Official organization established in 1972, in Cebu, Philippines.
